questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the classification of economic activities in India's national accounts:
1. Construction is grouped with industry and not with services.
2. Real estate, ownership of dwellings and professional services are grouped with financial services.
3. Public administration and defence are excluded from the services sector.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Construction belongs to industry (secondary) along with mining, manufacturing and utilities. Services cover trade-hotels-transport-communication, financial-real estate-professional services, and public administration-defence-other services, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Sectors of the Economy); MoSPI National Accounts classification

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT classified under the services sector in India's GVA estimates?
o: Trade, hotels, transport, communication and broadcasting services
Public administration, defence and other services
Financial, real estate and professional services
Electricity, gas, water supply and other utility services
questions.e: National accounts place electricity, gas, water supply and other utilities in industry along with mining, manufacturing and construction. The other three heads together make up the services sector.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Sectors of the Economy)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Remittances sent home by Indian workers abroad are not counted as India's services exports in the balance of payments.
Statement-II: Personal remittances are recorded as current transfers (secondary income) and not as payment for a service rendered.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Services exports record payment for services supplied to non-residents (software, travel, transport). Remittances are one-way transfers with no service in return, so they sit under private transfers in the current account; this is why they are classified separately even though they are large.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Balance of Payments); RBI BoP classification

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Special Economic Zones (SEZs) in India:
1. India's SEZ policy was first announced in the Export-Import Policy of April 2000.
2. Under the SEZ Act, 2005, an SEZ is treated as foreign territory for trade operations, duties and tariffs.
3. Kandla, set up in 1965, was the first export processing zone in Asia.
4. The Board of Approval for SEZs is chaired by the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The SEZ policy dates to April 2000 (EXIM Policy), the 2005 Act gave it statutory backing with a duty-free, foreign-territory character, and Kandla (1965) was Asia's first EPZ. The Board of Approval is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Commerce, not the Minister, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Foreign Trade); Ministry of Commerce, SEZ Act 2005

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Platform)
A. Account Aggregator
B. ONDC
C. BBPS
D. GeM
List-II (Description)
1. Consent-based sharing of financial data between regulated entities
2. Open-protocol network for e-commerce promoted under the Commerce Ministry
3. Interoperable bill-payment system operated by NPCI
4. Online marketplace for public procurement
questions.e: Account Aggregators move data only with the user's consent, ONDC is an open network meant to unbundle platform-based e-commerce, BBPS (Bharat Bill Payment System) is run by NPCI, and GeM is the government's procurement portal.
questions.s: RBI AA Master Direction; DPIIT; NPCI; GeM portal

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS):
1. Supply of a service from one country into another by electronic means is covered under Mode 1.
2. Mode 2 refers to the establishment of a commercial presence of a foreign supplier in the importing country.
3. Mode 4 covers only the temporary movement of natural persons and does not cover those seeking permanent employment or citizenship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Mode 1 is cross-border supply, Mode 2 is consumption abroad (the consumer travels) and Mode 3 is commercial presence, so statement 2 swaps Modes 2 and 3. Mode 4 is limited to temporary movement of service suppliers, which is why migration is outside GATS.
questions.s: WTO GATS text; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Foreign Trade)

questions.q: An Indian IT firm sends a team of engineers to a client's office in Germany for a six-month project. Under the GATS classification, this is an example of
questions.e: The service is delivered by individuals who travel temporarily to the importing country, which is Mode 4. It is not Mode 3 because no subsidiary or office is established, and not Mode 1 because the service is not delivered across the border electronically.
questions.s: WTO GATS; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Foreign Trade)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a statutory body created under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
2. NASSCOM is the industry association of the IT-BPM sector and was set up in 1988.
3. STPI was established in 1991 as an autonomous society under the electronics and IT ministry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: STPI predates the IT Act by almost a decade: it was set up in 1991 as an autonomous society under the then Department of Electronics (now MeitY), so it is not a creature of the IT Act. NASSCOM is a non-profit industry body, not a regulator.
questions.s: MeitY / STPI; NASSCOM; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Telecommunications Act, 2023:
1. It repeals the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885.
2. The Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933 continues to remain in force alongside it.
3. It also repeals the Telegraph Wires (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1950.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act replaces the colonial-era telecom statutes: the Telegraph Act 1885, the Wireless Telegraphy Act 1933 and the Telegraph Wires (Unlawful Possession) Act 1950 are all repealed. So statement 2 is wrong. The TRAI Act 1997 is amended, not repealed.
questions.s: PRS Legislative Research, Telecommunications Bill 2023 summary

questions.q:
As per the consolidated FDI policy, consider the following statements:
1. 100 per cent FDI is permitted in single-brand product retail trading under the automatic route.
2. Multi-brand retail trading allows FDI up to 51 per cent with government approval.
3. Foreign-owned e-commerce companies may hold inventory of goods sold on their platform under the inventory model.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Single-brand retail is on the automatic route up to 100 per cent and multi-brand retail is capped at 51 per cent through the government route. For e-commerce, FDI is allowed only in the marketplace model; foreign-owned entities cannot own inventory, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: DPIIT, Consolidated FDI Policy; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Foreign Investment)

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India derives its specific power to authorise and regulate payment systems such as card networks and UPI from which one of the following?
questions.e: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007 designates the RBI as the authority to authorise, regulate and supervise payment systems. The IT Act deals with electronic records and cyber law, and FEMA with foreign exchange.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking); RBI

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Unified Payments Interface was launched in 2016 and is operated by the National Payments Corporation of India.
2. The RuPay card network was launched by NPCI in 2012.
3. The BHIM app was launched in 2014.
4. NPCI is a wholly owned subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UPI (April 2016) and RuPay (2012) are NPCI products. BHIM came in December 2016, after demonetisation, not 2014. NPCI is a not-for-profit company promoted by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association with banks as shareholders, not an RBI subsidiary.
questions.s: NPCI; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Account Aggregators in India:
1. They can read and store a customer's financial data to offer analytics services.
2. They are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India as a class of NBFC.
3. Financial data flows through them only with the explicit consent of the customer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Account Aggregators are licensed by the RBI as NBFC-AA and act as consent managers. They are 'data-blind': they pass encrypted data between the provider and the user of the data without reading or storing it, so statement 1 is wrong.
questions.s: RBI Master Direction on NBFC-Account Aggregators

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The RBI introduced a regulatory sandbox framework in 2019 for live testing of new financial products under relaxed regulatory requirements.
2. The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) was established in 2020 under a 2019 Act.
3. IFSCA is headquartered at GIFT City in Gandhinagar, Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The sandbox lets FinTech firms test products on a limited scale with relaxed norms. IFSCA is the single regulator for financial services in IFSCs and has its headquarters in GIFT City, India's first operational IFSC.
questions.s: RBI; IFSCA; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking)

questions.q: India's retail Central Bank Digital Currency (e-rupee) is best described as
o: a stablecoin issued by a consortium of private banks
a decentralised cryptocurrency mined on a public blockchain
a digital form of legal tender issued by the Reserve Bank of India
a balance in a commercial bank's savings deposit shown in a wallet
questions.e: A CBDC is a direct liability of the central bank and is legal tender in digital form. It is different from private cryptocurrencies, which have no sovereign backing, and from bank deposits, which are liabilities of commercial banks.
questions.s: RBI concept note on CBDC; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Money and Banking)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding payments banks in India:
1. They can extend small loans up to Rs 1 lakh to individuals.
2. They can issue debit cards but cannot issue credit cards.
3. They must invest a major portion of their demand deposit balances in government securities eligible for SLR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Payments banks accept deposits (limit Rs 2 lakh per customer) and offer remittances and debit cards, but they cannot lend or issue credit cards. At least 75 per cent of demand deposit balances must be held in SLR-eligible government securities, so statement 1 is wrong.
questions.s: RBI Guidelines for Licensing of Payments Banks; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking)

questions.q: The idea of payments banks in India was recommended by which of the following committees?
o: Working Group on Microfinance (Y. H. Malegam)
Committee on Comprehensive Financial Services for Small Businesses and Low-Income Households (Nachiket Mor)
Committee on Financial Sector Reforms (Raghuram Rajan)
questions.e: The Nachiket Mor Committee (2013-14) proposed payments banks to widen financial inclusion. The Narasimham Committee dealt with banking sector reform, the Rajan Committee (2007-08) with financial sector reform, and Malegam with microfinance regulation.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking)

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
1. Enactment of the State Bank of India Act
2. Constitution of the Narasimham Committee on the financial system
3. Nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks
4. Nationalisation of the Reserve Bank of India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949, the SBI Act came in 1955 (taking over the Imperial Bank), 14 banks were nationalised in 1969, and the Narasimham Committee was set up in 1991 as part of the reforms.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking); Spectrum/Bipan Chandra for context

questions.q: Following the bank amalgamations effective April 2020, the number of public sector banks in India became
questions.e: Four mergers effective 1 April 2020 (PNB with OBC and United Bank, Canara with Syndicate, Union Bank with Andhra and Corporation, Indian Bank with Allahabad) reduced the number of PSBs from 18 to 12.
questions.s: Ministry of Finance announcement; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about small finance banks (SFBs) in India is correct?
o: They can be set up only by foreign banks
They can accept only demand deposits and are barred from lending
They are exempt from maintaining CRR and SLR
At least 75 per cent of their adjusted net bank credit must go to priority sector lending
questions.e: SFBs are meant to serve small businesses, farmers and low-income groups, so they carry a 75 per cent priority-sector target. Unlike payments banks they lend, and they must maintain CRR and SLR like other banks.
questions.s: RBI Guidelines for Licensing of Small Finance Banks; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding insurance in India:
1. Life insurance was nationalised in 1969 along with 14 commercial banks.
2. The general insurance business was nationalised in 1972.
3. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority was set up under a 1999 Act of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: LIC was formed in 1956 when life insurance was nationalised, not in 1969. General insurance was nationalised in 1972 (GIC and its subsidiaries), and the IRDA Act 1999 ended the public-sector monopoly and created the regulator.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Insurance); IRDAI

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha (Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025 (in force since February 2026):
1. It raises the ceiling on foreign investment in Indian insurance companies from 74 per cent to 100 per cent, subject to prescribed conditions.
2. It amends the Insurance Act, 1938, the Life Insurance Corporation Act, 1956 and the IRDA Act, 1999.
3. It repeals the Insurance Act, 1938 and replaces it with a new code.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act amends three existing laws and lifts the FDI cap from 74 to 100 per cent; it does not repeal the 1938 Act, so statement 3 is wrong. It also gives LIC more operational autonomy.
questions.s: India Briefing, 'India's New Insurance FDI Framework Takes Effect from February 5, 2026'; PRS

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding tourism promotion in India:
1. The Incredible India campaign was launched in 2002.
2. The PRASAD scheme for pilgrimage destinations is run by the Ministry of Culture.
3. The Swadesh Darshan scheme supports the integrated development of theme-based tourist circuits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PRASAD is a Ministry of Tourism scheme, like Swadesh Darshan, so statement 2 is wrong. Incredible India was the 2002 branding campaign.
questions.s: Ministry of Tourism; Nitin Singhania/Ramesh Singh

questions.q: The Travel and Tourism Development Index, which replaced the Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Index, is published by
o: the World Travel and Tourism Council
questions.e: The WEF introduced the Travel & Tourism Development Index to replace its earlier Competitiveness Index, with a focus on sustainability and resilience. WTTC publishes economic-impact research, not this index.
questions.s: World Economic Forum TTDI report

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the UDAN scheme:
1. It is the Regional Connectivity Scheme under the National Civil Aviation Policy, 2016.
2. Airlines flying on notified regional routes receive viability gap funding financed through a levy on certain domestic flights.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Tourism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) is the Ministry of Civil Aviation's regional connectivity scheme. A Regional Connectivity Fund built from a levy on certain domestic flights supports the viability gap funding, so statement 3 about the Tourism ministry is wrong.
questions.s: Ministry of Civil Aviation; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Logistics Performance Index is published by the World Economic Forum.
2. The National Logistics Policy, 2022 aims to bring India among the top 25 countries in the Logistics Performance Index by 2030.
3. The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan was launched in 2021 as a digital platform for integrated infrastructure planning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The LPI is a World Bank publication, so statement 1 is wrong. The NLP (September 2022) sets the 2030 target of a top-25 LPI rank, and Gati Shakti (October 2021) is a GIS-based platform to synchronise infrastructure projects across ministries.
questions.s: DPIIT, National Logistics Policy 2022; PIB

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Export of services is exempt from GST in a way that denies exporters any refund of input tax credit.
2. GST was introduced through the 101st Constitutional Amendment.
3. Service tax was introduced in India in 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Exports are 'zero-rated' under the IGST Act, which means no tax on the output and the exporter can claim a refund of input tax credit; they are not simply exempt. GST came through the 101st Amendment (2016) and was preceded by service tax from 1994.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Taxation)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: A Services PMI reading above 50 indicates that services activity has expanded compared with the previous month.
Statement-II: The PMI is a diffusion index built from a monthly survey of purchasing managers on changes in output, orders and employment.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A diffusion index counts how many respondents report an increase versus a decrease, with 50 as the no-change mark. That construction is why a value above 50 signals month-on-month expansion.
questions.s: S&P Global / HSBC India Services PMI methodology

questions.q: A Global Capability Centre (GCC) differs from a business process outsourcing vendor mainly because it
o: operates only within Special Economic Zones
is an in-house unit owned and operated by the parent multinational and serves only its own group
is a third-party contractor serving many unrelated clients
is a government-run facility that supports small exporters
questions.e: GCCs are captive centres that handle functions such as engineering, analytics and finance for the parent, and increasingly higher-value R&D. A BPO vendor is a third-party provider, and GCCs are not restricted to SEZs.
questions.s: NASSCOM; Ministry of Electronics and IT

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's trade in services:
1. The RBI publishes monthly data on India's international trade in services.
2. Software exports are included in the merchandise export data compiled by DGCI&S.
3. Travel receipts in the balance of payments represent spending by Indians travelling abroad.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: RBI compiles monthly services trade data. Software exports are services and appear in BoP services data, not merchandise data. Travel receipts record spending by foreign visitors in India; Indians' spending abroad is a payment.
questions.s: RBI monthly data on India's trade in services; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) in India:
1. They cannot accept demand deposits.
2. Their depositors are not covered by deposit insurance from the DICGC.
3. They are not part of the payment and settlement system and cannot issue cheques drawn on themselves.
4. They are registered and regulated by the RBI under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: These are the standard differences between banks and NBFCs: no demand deposits, no DICGC cover and no cheque-drawing facility on themselves. NBFCs are registered with and regulated by the RBI under Chapter IIIB of the RBI Act.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Narasimham Committee on the Financial System (1991):
1. It recommended a phased reduction in the statutory liquidity ratio.
2. It recommended a reduction of directed credit and a narrower priority sector.
3. It proposed the concept of narrow banking for weak banks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 1991 report pushed financial liberalisation: lower SLR and CRR and less directed credit. Narrow banking and consolidation of banks were ideas of the second Narasimham Committee (1998), so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Unified Payments Interface (UPI):
1. UPI was built on top of the IMPS infrastructure.
2. A single UPI app can be linked to accounts in multiple banks.
3. Both the payer and the payee must hold accounts in the same bank.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UPI is an interoperable layer over IMPS that lets one mobile app access accounts in different banks using a virtual payment address. Same-bank accounts are not needed, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: NPCI; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), with which India's Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement came into force on 1 October 2025?
questions.e: EFTA has four members: Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland. Sweden is a member of the European Union, not EFTA.
questions.s: EFTA joint communique, 1 Oct 2025

questions.q:
In the current account of India's balance of payments, 'invisibles' include which of the following?
1. Services
2. Transfers
3. Income
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: Merchandise trade is the 'visible' item. Invisibles cover trade in services, transfers (including remittances) and income (compensation of employees and investment income). FDI and portfolio flows belong to the capital and financial account.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Balance of Payments)

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
1. Launch of the Unified Payments Interface
2. Enactment of the Information Technology Act
3. Enactment of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act
4. Launch of the Digital India programme
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The IT Act came in 2000, Digital India was launched in July 2015, UPI went live in April 2016, and the DPDP Act was passed in August 2023.
questions.s: MeitY; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023:
1. It uses the terms Data Principal and Data Fiduciary.
2. It classifies personal data into sensitive and critical categories with separate rules.
3. It provides for the establishment of a Data Protection Board of India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act speaks of Data Principals (individuals) and Data Fiduciaries (entities deciding the purpose of processing) and creates a Data Protection Board. The sensitive/critical data categories belonged to earlier bill drafts and are not in the 2023 Act.
questions.s: MeitY; PRS Legislative Research

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC):
1. It is based on open protocols that allow buyer apps and seller apps to transact across networks.
2. It is an initiative promoted by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
3. It holds inventory and sells goods directly to consumers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ONDC is a network, not a marketplace: it standardises how buyers and sellers discover and transact on any compatible app. It does not hold stock or sell, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: DPIIT; ONDC

questions.q: Appeals against the directions and decisions of the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India lie before which one of the following?
o: The concerned High Court as the first appellate forum
Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal
questions.e: TDSAT was set up in 2000 by amending the TRAI Act to adjudicate disputes and hear appeals from TRAI and the licensor. Appeals from TDSAT go to the Supreme Court.
questions.s: TRAI Act 1997 as amended in 2000; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Services contribute more than half of India's gross value added, yet agriculture employs a larger share of the workforce than services do.
Statement-II: Many high-value services such as IT-BPM and finance are skill-intensive and generate relatively few jobs per unit of output.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The mismatch between GVA share and employment share is linked to the skill and capital intensity of the fastest-growing services, which cannot absorb the large pool of low-skilled agricultural workers. Employment data are from PLFS.
questions.s: Economic Survey; PLFS

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020:
1. They are framed under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
2. They are framed under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
3. They require e-commerce entities to display the country of origin of goods offered for sale.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Rules were notified under the Consumer Protection Act 2019 and cover marketplace and inventory e-commerce entities, including disclosure of country of origin. They were not framed under the IT Act, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: Department of Consumer Affairs; Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules 2020

questions.q:
Match the scheme with the Ministry responsible:
List-I (Scheme)
A. UDAN
B. Swadesh Darshan
C. Sagarmala
D. Digital India
List-II (Ministry)
1. Ministry of Tourism
2. Ministry of Civil Aviation
3. Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
4. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.e: UDAN is a regional air connectivity scheme, Swadesh Darshan develops tourist circuits, Sagarmala is port-led development, and Digital India is coordinated by MeitY.
questions.s: Respective ministries; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding insurance indicators:
1. Insurance penetration is the ratio of premium underwritten in a year to GDP.
2. Insurance density is the ratio of premium underwritten to GDP.
3. Insurance density is premium per capita.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Penetration measures premiums against the size of the economy, while density measures premium per person. Statement 2 wrongly gives the definition of penetration for density.
questions.s: IRDAI Annual Report; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy
questions.h: Penetration = % of GDP; Density = Per head

questions.q: NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL) is
o: the international arm of NPCI created to take UPI and RuPay to other countries
a body of the BRICS grouping to settle trade in local currencies
a subsidiary of the RBI for managing foreign exchange reserves
questions.e: NIPL is a wholly owned subsidiary of NPCI that has signed arrangements to link UPI and RuPay with payment systems abroad, which is how Indian tourists can pay by UPI in partner countries.
questions.s: NPCI

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. SEBI was established in 1988 as a non-statutory body and was given statutory powers by an Act of 1992.
2. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority became a statutory regulator through an Act passed in 1999.
3. The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority was set up in 2003 and obtained statutory status through an Act of 2013.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three regulators began or were strengthened in stages: SEBI (1988, SEBI Act 1992), IRDA (IRDA Act 1999) and PFRDA (interim authority in 2003, PFRDA Act 2013).
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Financial Markets and Regulators)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India Post Payments Bank can accept deposits but cannot extend loans directly.
Statement-II: India Post Payments Bank operates under a payments bank licence from the RBI.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Payments banks are barred from lending, which is why IPPB offers savings and current accounts and payment services but partners with other lenders for credit. IPPB began operations in September 2018 under the Department of Posts.
questions.s: RBI Payments Bank guidelines; Department of Posts

questions.q:
Match the institution or law with the year:
List-I
A. State Bank of India Act
B. Nationalisation of life insurance (LIC)
C. IRDA Act
D. Payment and Settlement Systems Act
List-II
1. 1955
2. 1956
3. 1999
4. 2007
questions.e: The SBI Act (1955) took over the Imperial Bank, LIC was created in 1956, the IRDA Act of 1999 opened insurance and created the regulator, and the PSS Act of 2007 governs payment systems.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (Banking, Insurance)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC):
1. LIC was listed on the stock exchanges through an initial public offering in 2022.
2. The Government of India continued to hold the majority of LIC's shares after the offering.
3. The LIC Act, 1956 was repealed to enable the listing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: LIC's IPO was in May 2022 and the Government sold only a small stake, so it remained the majority owner. The LIC Act 1956 was amended (to allow the listing), not repealed, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: Ministry of Finance / DIPAM; Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q:
Consider the following payment systems:
1. RTGS
2. NEFT
3. UPI
4. IMPS
How many of the above are operated by the Reserve Bank of India itself?
questions.e: RTGS and NEFT are owned and operated by the RBI. UPI and IMPS are retail payment systems operated by NPCI.
questions.s: RBI; NPCI

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the order of their introduction:
1. UPI
2. NEFT
3. RTGS
4. Pilot of the retail digital rupee
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: RTGS began in 2004 for large-value transfers, NEFT in 2005, UPI in 2016, and the retail e-rupee pilot in December 2022.
questions.s: RBI; NPCI
